Perchta Day (Perchtenlauf)

Perchta Day Celebration at Home

Celebrate Perchta Day by honoring the Alpine tradition of welcoming Frau Perchta with warmth, light, and festive foods. This agenda guides you through a day filled with symbolic activities and comforting treats.

  1. Morning

    Prepare Traditional Treats

    Start the day by making dumplings and poppy seed pastries to share with guests and performers, honoring the custom of offering these foods during the festival.

    Recipes: Traditional Dumplings · Poppy Seed Pastries

  2. Late Morning

    Decorate with Light and Symbols

    Decorate your home with candles and symbols of winter protection to invite Frau Perchta’s blessing and to chase away darkness, reflecting the spirit of the Perchtenlauf.

  3. Afternoon

    Create Masks and Bells

    Craft simple masks and prepare cowbells to emulate the Perchten figures who parade through villages, symbolizing the driving away of evil spirits.

  4. Early Evening

    Host a Perchtenlauf Parade at Home

    Organize a small procession around your home or yard, ringing bells and carrying torches or lanterns to mimic the traditional Perchtenlauf and celebrate light overcoming darkness.

  5. Evening

    Serve Milky Punch and Mulled Wine

    Warm up with milky punch and mulled wine, beverages traditionally enjoyed during the festivities, to toast the protection of the hearth and fields.

    Recipes: Milky Punch · Mulled Wine

  6. Night

    Enjoy Sweet Krapfen and Share Stories

    End the day by enjoying sweet krapfen with family or friends while sharing stories of Alpine folklore and the legend of Frau Perchta, keeping the tradition alive.

    Recipes: Krapfen

As the night settles, reflect on the warmth and protection of the season, carrying Frau Perchta’s blessings into the year ahead.
